change_summary: PLOS ONE issued an Expression of Concern about this paper, to inform readers of unresolved issues. Fig. 7 does not match its legend and text and has no LSD1 siRNA data, so a stated migration result is unsupported; the notice also notes a possible discontinuity in Fig. 4 and insufficient control detail for the transfection experiments. Similarities with other groups' work call into question the validity and provenance of the results, and the authors did not respond. This is an expression of concern, not a retraction, so the findings are in doubt but the paper has not been withdrawn.
evaluation: Your Section 2 cites [12] for higher LSD1 in tumour than normal lung tissue in 80 resected samples, and the stored paper reports that finding. The notice questions the validity and provenance of the results in general, but it names no problem with the tissue data, so it is unclear whether this background use is touched. Your Section 3 cites [12] for reduced H460 migration after LSD1 siRNA and takes it as the clearest sign that LSD1 drives migration, while the notice says Fig. 7 has no LSD1 siRNA data and so that result is not supported. This use is touched, and because it underpins your central hypothesis the overall impact is medium.
recommendation: PLOS ONE issued an Expression of Concern about the paper, and the notice says Fig. 7 does not report data for an LSD1 siRNA experiment, so the migration result statement is not supported. Your Section 3 takes the H460 knockdown migration result as the clearest indication that LSD1 drives migration, so that use is touched. Hedge or replace that Section 3 claim, cite the notice next to [12], and don't build new work on this result. Whether your Section 2 tissue-expression use is touched is unclear, because the notice questions the results only in general terms; add a light hedge or an independent source there.
